# EnterpriseGlue v0.20.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.19.2`.

## Highlights

- **cloud-release-affinity:** Adds release-aware placement v3, tenant-scoped mixed-release SSO callbacks, short-lived tenant Cloud identity, plugin work handoff, plugin release-affinity declarations, and a trusted system frontend boundary for managed SaaS.
- **release-and-deployment:** Publishes the signed OSS distribution lock as an immutable OCI subject that downstream Cloud release manifests can pin and verify.
- **plugin-installation-toolchain:** Keeps the plugin installer, runtime, RBAC, and Plugin Manager Helm chart versions aligned for protected release-candidate qualification and publication.
- **plugin-installation-toolchain:** Rebuilds the plugin-installer and Plugin Manager images with credential-scoping fixes from ORAS 1.3.4 and the patched golang.org/x/crypto dependency floor required by the container vulnerability gate.
- **release-pipeline:** Keeps successful Helm chart comparison diagnostics out of release-candidate subject references during idempotent staging retries.
- **release-pipeline:** Configures authenticated GitHub Packages reads while staging immutable release candidates so package publication planning can complete before a release merges.
- **release-pipeline:** Mounts the repository vulnerability exception policy into the protected Trivy container so exact release-candidate image scans can run fail closed.

## User and administrator impact

- Managed deployments can expose tenant administration pages from a release-neutral control plane without packaging those pages as an optional tenant marketplace plugin.
- Existing OSS, EE, and native marketplace plugin behavior remains unchanged when no system frontend modules are configured.
- Managed pooled deployments can bind each request to the exact tenant, shard, release, placement epoch, and release-assignment epoch without changing tenant SSO ownership.
- Managed mixed-release deployments can keep each tenant's OIDC or SAML callback and asynchronous plugin work on that tenant's assigned release.
- SaaS composition can reference the real v0.20.0 OSS distribution lock by digest instead of relying on a placeholder subject or a mutable download URL.
- The plugin toolchain can be staged and published as one coherent set instead of failing release qualification because package and chart versions differ.
- The v0.20.0 plugin toolchain candidate no longer contains the critical golang.org/x/crypto finding reported in the embedded ORAS and Cosign binaries.
- ORAS registry client certificates, custom headers, and debug traces receive the upstream 1.3.4 credential-scoping protections before the first public v0.20.0 toolchain release.
- Protected release retries can reuse an equivalent staged chart without corrupting the immutable reference passed to Cosign.
- Protected releases can stage the signed plugin package, image, and chart candidate without failing when the package planner checks existing GitHub Packages versions.
- Protected releases no longer fail because the containerized candidate scan cannot read the checked-in Trivy ignore policy.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Managed operators may add same-origin trusted system module descriptors to the existing frontend runtime configuration document.
- Managed mixed-release shards set EG_TENANT_PLACEMENT_RELEASE_ID, EG_TENANT_CLOUD_IDENTITY_AUDIENCE, and the secret EG_TENANT_RELEASE_CONTROLLER_TOKEN; self-hosted deployments leave them unset.
- Register tenant-scoped OIDC and SAML callback URLs before opening Preview enrollment; the established global callbacks remain supported for existing deployments.
- Resolve and verify ghcr.io/enterpriseglue/releases/enterpriseglue-oss-distribution:v0.20.0, then record its digest-pinned subject in the SaaS release manifest.
- Use plugin runtime and installer RBAC charts 0.2.7 with @enterpriseglue/plugin-installer 0.2.7, and use the Plugin Manager chart 0.1.7 with @enterpriseglue/plugin-manager 0.1.7.
- Use the v0.20.0 plugin installer 0.2.7 and Plugin Manager 0.1.7 images and their matching charts; do not deploy an earlier release-candidate image digest.

## API and integration compatibility

- The enterprise frontend plugin API exports additive trusted system module descriptor and module contracts.
- The frontend host can activate multiple owner-isolated system modules in addition to the existing singular EE compatibility bridge.
- Placement assertion v3 and the tenant Cloud identity endpoint are additive; placement v1 and v2 remain supported.
- Plugin manifest v1 accepts an optional releaseAffinity declaration for mixed-host, fallback, job, and event compatibility.
- Tenant-scoped OIDC and SAML callback routes and the workload-only release-assignment route are additive; global callback routes remain available.

## Configuration

- The optional systemFrontendModules runtime-config field declares reverse-DNS owner ids, same-origin JavaScript entry paths, and SHA-256 integrity values.
- A configured module marked required fails application startup when its descriptor, integrity check, import, or activation fails; optional modules fail closed without affecting the OSS shell.
- Managed release hosts require an exact release ID, Cloud identity audience, and dedicated private release-controller token.

## Database migrations

- Migration: 1700000000130-add-release-aware-plugin-work.
- The additive migration stores nullable release ID and assignment epoch on plugin event deliveries and scheduled jobs, and adds one tenant release-work assignment row per managed tenant.
- Existing rows and unmanaged deployments remain valid because the new event/job columns are nullable and the assignment table is unused without a managed release ID.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- System module entry URLs must resolve to the application origin and each downloaded module is verified against a configured SHA-256 digest before import.
- Owner identifiers and extension keys are validated and cross-owner collisions fail atomically.
- System modules receive the existing constrained host context and cannot register legacy feature or component replacements.
- Tenant Cloud identity assertions are short lived and contain tenant, role, shard, release, and epoch claims but no SSO provider configuration, identity assertion, or secret.
- The release-work handoff uses a dedicated constant-time bearer check, requires an exact configured host release, rejects stale epochs, and does not accept interactive or ordinary service-account tokens.
- The protected release workflow compares any existing semantic OCI tag with the generated lock bytes and fails closed on a mismatch.
- The digest-pinned distribution subject is signed and verified with the plugin-toolchain workflow identity before release completion.
- Release qualification continues to fail closed unless package, chart, and image version subjects form a coordinated immutable toolchain.
- Updates embedded ORAS from 1.3.3 to the upstream 1.3.4 security release that scopes mTLS certificates and custom headers to the configured registry origin and redacts replayable credentials from debug traces.
- Compiles both ORAS 1.3.4 and Cosign 3.1.3 with golang.org/x/crypto 0.55.0 so CVE-2026-56854 is absent from the shipped binaries.
- Both production Dockerfiles verify the selected x/crypto module version from each compiled binary, and the HIGH/CRITICAL Trivy gate remains fail closed.
- The candidate workflow still verifies the canonical Helm payload before signing the exact immutable chart subject.
- Candidate staging uses the job-scoped GitHub token through the generated npm configuration and retains the existing packages permission boundary.
- The release remains fail closed when registry authentication or immutable package comparison fails.
- The scanner receives the read-only policy file at an explicit container path and still rejects every non-ignored vulnerability severity.
- Candidate publication remains blocked when the policy file is absent, unreadable, or the scan fails.

## Known limitations

- Content Security Policy must permit the host's integrity-verified module import mechanism when system modules are enabled.
- The OSS repository provides the neutral extension mechanism; managed release policy, tenant lifecycle, and control-plane APIs remain deployment-owned concerns.

## Rollback

- Remove systemFrontendModules from runtime configuration or roll back the frontend image; deployments without the field retain the previous startup path.
- The publication is additive and does not alter application runtime behavior; recover the same release workflow against the same tag and source revision if publication is interrupted.
- Before publication, revert the chart metadata and matching package-version changes together; after immutable publication, correct any artifact defect with a new forward version.
- Do not restore an earlier release-candidate plugin-installer or Plugin Manager image because it fails the current critical-vulnerability policy; roll back the complete v0.20.0 candidate instead.
- Revert the workflow output redirection; no application, API, configuration, or database state changes are involved.
- Revert the workflow configuration to disable candidate staging; no public release tag or production package version is created by the staging workflow.
- Revert the workflow mount to disable the correction; no application, API, configuration, or database state changes are involved.
